page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.large is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned as a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instruction sets. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of general purpose workloads. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage attachments, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Performance evaluation reflects a distinct divergence between single-threaded capability and aggregate capacity. In single-core testing, the instance records middle-tier results, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 1371.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1843.79, and 27.3 GB/s during single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, multi-core and throughput-heavy tests place the instance in lower benchmark percentiles due to the two-thread ceiling. PassMark CPU scores reach 2719.23, and multi-core Geekbench totals 1586.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 104.76 GB/s for cached operations but drops to 14.71 GB/s for large uncached blocks. Real-world workload benchmarks echo these hardware constraints, with Redis SET operations achieving 1.94 million operations per second and static web throughput measuring 2.46 GB/s.

From an economic standpoint, the instance delivers predictable single-thread execution at an entry-level resource footprint. The inclusion of dedicated vCPUs avoids performance throttling common in burstable CPU models, though absolute throughput remains constrained by the two-thread limit and lack of integrated local NVMe storage. The ecs.u1-c1m4.large matches low-traffic web applications, API endpoints, microservices, development and staging servers, and background automation tasks where predictable CPU timing and moderate memory density are needed without heavy parallel compute demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.large is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, while offering no bundled local storage and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-thread performance across synthetic and compression tests, supported by AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. However, multi-threaded metrics, including PassMark CPU and multi-core Geekbench, place in the lowest quartile due to the two-thread limit. Memory throughput and application benchmarks such as Redis operations and static web serving reflect similar entry-tier constraints. With low per-resource cost overhead and dedicated core allocation, the ecs.u1-c1m4.large provides functional efficiency for low-throughput web servers, microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight background workers, and staging environments.
